details: Renewed military strikes between the US and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz on May 25-26, reported on May 28, led to a sharp risk-off sentiment across global financial markets. US forces targeted Iranian missile sites and vessels, while Iran's Revolutionary Guard reportedly retaliated against a US airbase. This escalation threatened a fragile ceasefire, causing Bitcoin to fall below $73,000 and triggering nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto liquidations as investors sought safer assets. Oil prices also surged in response to the increased tensions in the critical shipping corridor.
title: US-Iran Strikes Escalate in Hormuz, Bitcoin Plunges

details: On May 29, optimism grew for a potential agreement between the United States and Iran to extend their ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz for commercial shipping. While the deal awaited President Trump's approval, the prospect of de-escalation led to a positive shift in global financial markets. European and Asian stock markets rose, and oil prices slipped as investor concerns over prolonged inflation and higher interest rates eased. This development suggests a cautious return of risk appetite, which could positively influence risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Hopes for US-Iran Ceasefire Deal Boost Global Markets
